title: How I Became Hindu
byline: by Sita Ram Goel · Voice of India · 1982, enlarged in 1993 with the chapter “Nightmare of Nehruism”
lede: Voice of India's publisher tells how he arrived at the positions found in most of the books on this shelf. He was born in a Haryana village into an Arya Samaj household and schooled among Jains. He became a Gandhian, then a Marxist, and by February 1948 was ready to join the Communist Party. His friend Ram Swarup talked him out of it. By 1949 he had become an anti-Communist writer, and by 1959 a “convinced and conscious Hindu”. The 1993 edition adds a long, bitter postscript on Nehru and Nehruism.
